title: The magi and the flight (Matthew 2:1–23)
hook: strangers from the east follow a star, then the family runs to Egypt as refugees

segments.voice: Yesterday, Simeon and Anna, their long waiting, and the Nunc Dimittis: waiting is not wasted. That's the week of the child: Elizabeth's doorway, Mary's song, Joseph's dream, no room, the shepherds, the Temple.
screen: `WAITING IS NOT WASTED.` → `THE WEEK OF THE CHILD.`

segments.voice: Strangers walk into Jerusalem from the east and ask a dangerous question in a king's city. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Where is he that is born king of the Jews? For we have seen his star in the east, and are come to adore him." King Herod is on the throne, and Matthew says that when he heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. Matthew tells the story from a different angle than Luke: no shepherds, no manger. His Greek calls the strangers magi; the Douay-Rheims says wise men. Some readers picture star-watchers from Persia or Babylon.
screen: `STRANGERS FROM THE EAST.` → `WHERE IS HE THAT IS BORN KING?` → `HEROD IS LISTENING.`

segments.voice: The star leads them to Bethlehem, to the house, and they find the child with his mother. They kneel and open their treasures: gold, frankincense and myrrh. Now, what Matthew doesn't say. He never says there were three; tradition counted three, likely from the three gifts. He never calls them kings; that came later, from psalms about kings bringing gifts. Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar are names from later tradition. Why they matter: they're the first people in Matthew's Gospel to worship Jesus, and they're foreigners, not from Israel at all. So the Church calls this feast the Epiphany, from the Greek for a showing, an appearing: Christ shown to the whole world, not just one people. Remember day nineteen: catholic, according to the whole. Here it is, at the very start. Then the story turns dark. The magi are warned in a dream not to go back to Herod. And Joseph, the man who never speaks, has another dream: "Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt." They leave by night, with whatever they can carry, across a border, into a foreign country. Herod, furious, orders the killing of the baby boys of Bethlehem; the Church remembers them as the Holy Innocents. The family stays in Egypt until Herod dies. So in Matthew, right after strangers worship him, Jesus's family becomes refugees. Pope Pius the Twelfth once called the Holy Family the model of every family forced to flee, and Catholics still pray for refugees in their name.
screen: `GOLD, FRANKINCENSE, AND MYRRH.` · `NOT THREE, NOT KINGS: MAGI.` · `EPIPHANY — SHOWN TO THE WORLD.` · `ARISE, AND FLY INTO EGYPT.` · then, large: `THE HOLY FAMILY WERE REFUGEES.`

segments.voice: Pray for one family that's had to leave home, the way Catholics do, in the name of the Holy Family: Jesus, Mary and Joseph. A mother carrying a child, a father carrying a bag, a border ahead and no idea what's on the other side. If prayer isn't yours, hold them in mind and hope for them.
Epiphany. A showing: Christ revealed to strangers from the east, the whole world, before his family runs for their lives.
Your line: the holy family were refugees. That's day twenty-eight: four weeks, done.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the Epiphany on January 6 or the nearest Sunday; in many places the door is blessed with chalk, and the Church remembers the Holy Innocents on December 28.

what it means: foreigners are the first to worship Jesus in Matthew, and then his family flees as refugees.
what a scholar hears: magoi, a word ancient writers used for Persian priestly star-watchers; kings from Psalm 71 (72) and Isaiah 60; Pius XII's Exsul Familia (1952) on the Holy Family in exile.

chat.meaning: Matthew's magi are foreigners from the east. Epiphany means a showing: Christ revealed to the whole world.

notes: Matthew 2:2 and 2:13 quoted from Douay-Rheims; confirm exact wording.
Magi as star-watchers from Persia or Babylon: common scholarly view; confirm.
Herod killing members of his own family (a wife and sons, per Josephus): stated simply; confirm.
The massacre of the innocents is recorded only in Matthew; mentioned briefly and without dramatization. Confirm.
Pius XII's Exsul Familia opens by calling the Holy Family in exile the archetype of every refugee family; paraphrased. Confirm.
The outline practice 'pray for one refugee family' is offered as an invitation with a non-praying alternative.
